summary.headline: Skipper Q2 FY27 revenue hit record INR1,384 crores (+10% YoY) and PAT rose 56% to INR57.5 crores, while management still targets 15% FY27 revenue growth.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record second-quarter revenue of INR1,384 crores (+10% YoY), EBITDA of INR145 crores (+11%, 10.5% margin) and PAT of INR57.5 crores (+56%, 4.2% margin). Q2 order inflow was a record INR2,111 crores (+70% YoY), with export inflow of INR1,055 crores, and the order book stood at INR10,066 crores. Export shipments fell 46% YoY to about INR106 crores because customers are deferring shipments amid high freight rates. Management kept FY27 revenue growth guidance of about 15% (at worst 13-14%), order inflow guidance of INR7,500 crores and export inflow guidance of INR1,500 crores.

segments.name: Infrastructure (EPC/projects)
segments.commentary: Management said Infra is the main driver of H1 revenue growth and will lead H2 growth; it carries lower EBITDA margins than Engineering, which analysts flagged as a margin-mix question.

segments.name: Engineering products
segments.commentary: Revenue growth was muted due to weak order inflows last year and export shipment deferrals. Management expects Engineering to grow in H2 and to even out across segments once new export orders execute next year.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Middle East now under 18% of export order book; North America about 44% and Australia about 18-19%, so developed markets are over 60%. Q2 export revenue fell 46% YoY to about INR106 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of about 15% maintained; management says at worst 13-14% given shipment deferrals.
FY27 order inflow target of INR7,500 crores maintained; export order inflow target of INR1,500 crores maintained, with about INR1,000-1,100 crores already secured.
Employee cost expected at about 5.5% of revenue in Q3 FY27, after Q2 included Q1 arrears.
Operating cash flow expected to be at least 75% of total cash flow this year.
Net working capital days to stay in a 90-100 day range; long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 12%, with 10-11% described as the interim range.
H1 margin expansion of about 20-30 bps; management says margin expansion may be lower than planned but margins will not decline.
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion of 75,000 MTPA (Phase 2, 375,000 to 450,000 MTPA) is on track for commissioning in H2 FY27, possibly end of Q3 or early Q4.
Longer-term roadmap of 600,000 MTPA by FY29; the next phase is likely greenfield and requires new land, with a location targeted for identification within the quarter.
Annual capex has been about INR250-300 crores, and the current expansion costs about the same; land cost may be added for greenfield projects.
Capacity utilisation was about 80% in Q2 on 375,000 MTPA; management says 90% is achievable but export deferrals are holding it back.
Preferential equity raise of about INR433.5 crores; CRISIL rating upgraded to A+/stable.
demand_pricing: Bidding pipeline above INR35,000 crores; management expects at least INR1 lakh crore of annual domestic transmission bidding through 2032-33.
Export shipments are being deferred by customers because freight rates are high; management believes freight has peaked.
Most new orders are fixed-price; management says firm-price orders carry a pricing buffer and higher down payments, so margin risk is low.
Export orders are mostly FOB; less than 25-30% of the export order book is CIF, so freight exposure is limited.
Management cites AI data-centre power transmission demand in the US, and a small acquisition in South India of about INR15-16 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% FY27 revenue growth target still achievable given H1 growth of about 7%, which implies about 21.6% in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is largely in line with 15%, and at worst the miss would be 1-2 points because of shipment deferrals; Q1 grew about 4-5% and Q2 about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the export order book is CIF and exposed to freight?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said less than 25-30% of the export order book is CIF, and the company has no risk from further freight escalation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the employee cost run-rate for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 was inflated by Q1 arrears paid with Q2 salaries; management expects Q3 employee cost at about 5.5% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual capex is INR250-300 crores; the current expansion costs about the same. Operating cash flow is expected to cover at least 75% of total cash flow, and debt-to-equity is 0.38x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the phasing and land status for the next capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 (to 450,000 MTPA) lands in H2 FY27; the greenfield site is being identified, with Phase 1 starting by end FY28 and full operation by FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working-capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital days were cut from about 200 to about 90 over 4-5 years; management expects 90-100 days to be stable and says export and domestic working capital are comparable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order inflow guidance achievable through exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept INR7,500 crores total and INR1,500 crores export inflow guidance, citing uncertain export order finalisation timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins hold at 10-11% in the interim?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes; cost pressure from fuel and commodities may limit expansion, but margins will not drop.

risks_watch: Export shipment deferrals tied to high freight rates and Middle East conflict; Middle East exposure is still about 18% of export order book.
H2 revenue must grow about 21.6% to reach 15% for FY27; management now says the figure could be 13-14%.
Input cost inflation (fuel, commodities) is limiting margin expansion relative to plan.
Greenfield expansion needs a site and land acquisition, which adds cost and timing risk beyond Phase 2 commissioning.
Export order finalisation timelines are uncertain, which affects whether INR1,500 crores export inflow is achieved.
Infra-led revenue growth carries lower segment margins; monitor mix in Q3 and Q4.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year outlook and margins, with clear caveats on export deferrals and cost pressure. Management was candid on Engineering growth being muted and gave a downside range for revenue. On margins, management was firm that they will not decline, but guided lower than earlier plans.
key_quotes: So I'd say that the new orders coming in, definitely are coming with good margins.
So I'd say that the risk to margin is nil because even in the first half of the year, despite the cost inflationary pressure has been there pretty much right from the beginning of this year.
So yes, we are facing shipment deferrals from a lot of customers who are waiting for the prices to come down.
We are in advanced stages of identification.

adds.what: Greenfield next phase to 600,000 MTPA by FY29; location not yet identified

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at ~15% (worst case 13-14%) with H1 revenue only +7%, so H2 must accelerate; backing is a INR10,066 crore order book and record Q2 orders of INR2,111 crore, plus 75,000 MTPA Phase 2 due H2 FY27, but export shipment deferrals (-46% YoY) and ~80% utilisation weigh on delivery.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 margin expansion guided at only about 20-30 bps and Q2 PAT margin rose 130 bps to 4.2%, but management says margins will not decline and input cost (fuel, commodities) pressure limits expansion versus plan, with EBITDA margin at 10.5% and interim range 10-11% against a 12% long-term aspiration.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Phase 2 (75,000 MTPA, 375,000 to 450,000 MTPA, about 20% of capacity, INR275 crore capex) is under construction and firmly guided for commissioning in H2 FY27, possibly end Q3 or early Q4; utilisation is about 80% on 375,000 MTPA.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue growth is guided at about 15% for FY27 (worst case 13-14%) versus H1 at +7%, so H2 must accelerate to roughly 21.6% at the 15% target; record Q2 order inflow of INR2,111 crores (+70% YoY) and an order book of INR10,066 crores support it, but export shipments fell 46% YoY to about INR106 crores on deferrals.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% with Phase 2 only coming online in H2 FY27, and the next greenfield phase to 600,000 MTPA by FY29 needs new land with a site to be identified within the quarter; annual capex is INR250-300 crores.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 revenue growth at about 15% with a downside to 13-14% due to shipment deferrals, and kept export inflow at INR1,500 crores with only about INR1,000-1,100 crores secured, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue grew only 7% and H2 must grow about 21.6% for the 15% target; management already flags a 1-2 point miss from export shipment deferrals (-46% YoY in Q2) and said margin expansion may be lower than planned.

rows.label: Record export order inflow converting to revenue next year
rows.why: Q2 export order inflow of INR1,055 crores already exceeds the full FY26 export inflow, and management expects Engineering to even out once these export orders execute next year; the order book is INR10,066 crores.

rows.label: Lower finance cost and debt after preferential raise
rows.why: Finance cost fell to 3.2% of revenue from 4.2% a year ago, gross debt is INR964 crores (down about INR358 crores YoY) and debt-to-equity is 0.38x from 0.64x after the INR433.5 crore preferential raise.

rows.label: Fixed-price order book and pricing buffer
rows.why: Most new orders are fixed-price but carry a pricing buffer and higher down payments, and less than 25-30% of the export book is CIF, so freight and input-cost exposure is limited.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 15% FY27 revenue guide (worst case 13-14%), Phase 2 commissioning and margins not declining, but cautious on export deferrals, fuel and commodity cost pressure; analysts pushed on the H2 growth required (~21.6%) and infra-led margin mix.
